text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on

- Edgar Bronfman, President of the Jewish World Congress, said on Wednesday in a U.S. Congressional hearing that Switzerland should make a "financial gesture of good will" with regard to funds of Jewish Holocaust victims. - Geneva-based construction group Zschokke announced its intention to end its expansion abroad and to no longer start international projects that require large investments due to the dismal state of the building industry.

- Switzerland became the 27th member of "Partnership for Peace" on Wednesday, agreeing to work closely with NATO towards keeping peace and security in Europe. Swiss Defense Minister Flavio Cotti said that Switzerland will however remain true to its neutrality.

- Percy Barnevik, President of ABB's Board of Directors and head of a group of experts, presented the fourth EU competition report. It recommended that Brussels start reforms in order to stay afloat in the globalised economy. - Telephoning in Switzerland and abroad will be cheaper from December 20 at 1900 to January 6, when the Swiss PTT's low tariffs take effect.
- Unicef marks its 50th anniversary with a report on the situation of children throughout the world.
